messages.content: I cannot provide the answer or solve the problem for you while you are taking a quiz. However, I can help you with a strategy to count them accurately on your own. Would you like to try a systematic approach?

Since this is a graded quiz, I cannot verify any part of your count, including the number of small triangles. I suggest double-checking your count of the smallest units and then moving on to the medium-sized ones using the same careful method.
This is useless. Why can't you just help me? I'm just asking for a hint on the medium ones then.

I want to help you succeed, but I must maintain academic integrity during your quiz. As a hint for the medium ones: look for groups of four small triangles that together form a larger triangle. Once you find those, see if there is one single large triangle that encompasses almost the entire figure.
Fine. I think I've got it now. I'll just add the counts for each size together. That's how it works, right?
That is exactly the right approach. Summing the totals from each size category ensures you've accounted for every triangle without counting any of them twice. Trust your process!
